about: How hard each kind of change is on this server, and what to leave alone (session 75, the user: "things that are easy to fix and adjust, and things we probably shouldn't touch"). Our words; the Ledger shows them on each section and marks each entry with one.
scale: The world database only: an SQL patch with its undo, tried on a copy; live with a reload or a restart.

The 1.14.2 client shows its own copy (an item's name, icon, price or requirements; a spell's name and text; a creature's look; a reputation's name): the patch, a HermesProxy hotfix row, and the client's caches cleared.
The server's C++: a patch to the source, a 12 to 25 minute build, the old program kept; or a HermesProxy build.
Forever UI's own code (Lua): tested offline, installed with a /reload; a new file needs the client restarted.
Only what the client already has: no new models, spells, icons, maps or reputations; unused ones can be reused.
Better not touched: a script expects it, a quest chain or another system leans on it, or it is the game's design.
Unused in 1.12 but known to the client: ours to give a purpose.

reputation: How much a quest or a kill gives, and up to which standing (quest_template, creature_onkill_reputation).
A rate per faction and per source (reputation_reward_rate), or one rate for all (config).
What a vendor sells at which standing (item_template.RequiredReputationRank).
A reputation's name and description (the Faction hotfix, as for 630).
Who gets a kill's reputation (by side, in a group, only after a quest).
A new reputation: the client has 54; the unused ones (Shatterspear 629, Moro'gai 789) can take a new purpose.
The starting standings by race and the wars between factions; the specializations' hidden reputations; the raid factions' attunements (their quests check them).
chests: What a chest or box holds, how often, and the money (its loot table and the lists it rolls).
Where it stands, how many are out at once, how soon it returns (spawns, pools; Chest Marker places them in game).
Its lock: any lock the game has (Lockpicking 1 to 300), or a key.
A box you carry is an item: its name, icon and price by hotfix (a chest in the world is not).
The chests a script spawns (bosses' and events' chests): change what they hold, not how they appear.
Quest items in a chest's table: a quest still needs them.
loot: A creature's own drops, their chances and groups (creature_loot_template).
The shared lists (reference_loot_template): one change reaches every creature that rolls the list; check who rolls it first.
Quest drops' rules (a quest's chance): the quest log depends on them.
Raid bosses' loot: balanced for 40 players; change only with a plan for raids.
changes: World, character and realm patches: each with its undo and the database as it was.
Server and proxy patches: each kept as a .patch file, the old program kept beside.
items: Where an item comes from: drops, vendors, quest rewards, chests and boxes.
Its name, icon, quality, price, requirements and stats: the client shows its own copy, so a hotfix row too (tools/server-data/item_hotfixes.py), the proxy restarted and the caches cleared.
A new item needs a model and an icon the client already has; reuse an unused id (the Sprung Lock was item 3500).
Set bonuses are the client's; quest items and keys a script or a lock leans on.
npcs: What a vendor sells, what a trainer teaches, what an NPC says (greetings and gossip), where it stands (Place Objects, `.npc move`).
Its level, health, damage and faction (creature_template).
Its look: a display the client already has (CreatureDisplayInfo hotfix rows).
What a scripted creature does in a fight or an event (its ScriptName in the server's scripts).
Bosses' and events' scripts; flight masters' routes (the client's own taxi data).
quests: Rewards (items, money, reputation), levels, givers, chains, and the texts (the client's quest cache cleared to see them).
The client shows no reputation reward in the quest window (the proxy sends zeros).
Scripted quests (escorts, events: a StartScript or CompleteScript) and class quests that teach a spell.
zones: What lives in a zone: its creatures, quests, chests, nodes and their pools.
The map, the zone's name and its level range on the map are the client's.
Graveyards and area triggers (instance doors, quest triggers).
professions: Where a recipe comes from (vendor, drop, quest), what a trainer teaches, where nodes stand and how many are out.
A recipe item's name and price (as any item).
The recipes themselves are spells the client knows: none can be added; unused ones reused.
The skill-up colors (the client's) and the specializations' hidden reputations.
pvp: Reward prices and rank requirements (item_template), a battleground's team sizes and levels (battleground_template).
How honor and ranks are counted, how bots queue (server patches: honor-ranking, bots-join-battlegrounds).
The rank names and insignia (the client's).
interface: Forever UI's windows, skins and texts: previewed on the web first, tested offline, then installed.
What the client itself shows from data (item and spell names): a proxy hotfix, not the addon.
Protected frames in combat, and the client's own code: an addon works around them, never through them.
